channel.description: Latest articles from West Hawaii Today (westhawaiitoday.com)

item.title: Drilling is underway to examine Antarctica’s melting ice from below
item.description: To peer into the future of one of Antarctica’s largest and fastest-shrinking glaciers, scientists Wednesday began piercing a deep hole through its icy core.

item.title: Senate passes deal to fund government and negotiate ICE limits
item.description: WASHINGTON — The Senate passed a bipartisan spending package Friday to fund most of the government and keep the Department of Homeland Security running for two weeks while Democrats and President Donald Trump negotiate restrictions on the administration’s immigration crackdown.

item.title: Protesters denounce Trump immigration tactics in ‘national shutdown’
item.description: They ditched school in Atlanta. Left work in Philadelphia. Blocked traffic in Los Angeles. And closed businesses in New York. Across the country Friday, protesters marched, rallied and disrupted their everyday routines in solidarity with Minneapolis residents to demand an end to the Trump administration’s immigration tactics.

item.title: Mahuna selected to be police chief
item.description: The Hawaii County Police Commission voted Friday to select Reed Mahuna as the next police chief.

item.title: Police ID man killed in car crash on Pauahi Street in Hilo
item.description: Police have identified the man who died in the single-vehicle collision that occurred early Thursday morning in Hilo as 20-year-old Jordan Grant of Hilo.

item.title: Justice Dept. releases 3 million pages of Epstein files
item.description: The Justice Department on Friday released 3 million more pages of documents along with thousands of videos and images from its Jeffrey Epstein files, as the Trump administration sought to bring an end to the accusations and speculation swirling around the case.

item.title: ‘It’s all just going down the toilet’: Police chiefs fume at ICE tactics
item.description: Five years ago, local police departments faced a tidal wave of criticism over racial profiling and the unnecessary killing of unarmed people. Many citizens looked to the federal government to rein them in.

item.title: Kamehameha Schools tuition to be free, judge rules
item.description: A Circuit Court probate judge Thursday granted the Kamehameha Schools trustees’ petition that will allow it to be tuition-free beginning in fall of the upcoming school year.

item.title: Tropical Gardening: Waimea Cherry Blossom Festival is Feb. 7
item.description: Spring flowering trees are on schedule to bloom, and most notable are the cherry blossoms of upland Waimea. To celebrate the blooming, check out the Waimea Cherry Blossom Festival next Saturday, Feb. 7. There will be all kinds of activities to showcase the age-old Japanese tradition of hanami.

item.title: Volcano Watch: When it rained rocks — tephra fall during Kilauea’s episode 41
item.description: Large lava fountains streamed from both the north and south vents reaching heights of at least 1475 feet (450 meters) during episode 41 of Kilauea’s summit eruption on Jan. 24, 2026. Strong updrafts coupled with light winds blowing to the east and north sent lava fragments from the fountains, called tephra, over much of the District of Puna and into South Hilo and the eastern edge of Ka‘u.
